name: Private School Affidavit (PSA / R-4)
deadline: Statutory filing period October 1-15 each year; CDE online system opens about August 1 and stays open through June 30, so a school starting mid-year files when it begins. Filing in August/September counts; no second October filing needed.
legal_basis: Ed Code 33190; Ed Code 48222
description: Online registration filed under penalty of perjury with the California Department of Education listing the school name/address, directors/officers, enrollment by grade and other required information. Filing is not a license or approval. Print/save the confirmation and keep a copy (CDE recommends retaining a copy). Schools opened in July must wait until the August filing period opens.

name: Copy of filed Private School Affidavit / confirmation
legal_basis: CDE PSA FAQ recommendation; Ed Code 48222 (district may verify affidavit before accepting the exemption)
description: Keep a printed or PDF copy of every year's affidavit. It is your proof of the compulsory attendance exemption if a district, truancy officer, or another school asks, and helps later with transcripts and records requests.

name: Attendance register
frequency: daily, kept for each school year
legal_basis: Ed Code 48222
description: A register of pupil attendance that clearly indicates every absence of a half day or more. A simple calendar or spreadsheet per student is sufficient. California sets no minimum number of days for private schools, but many families track 175-180 days.

name: Attendance records (PSP)
frequency: per PSP schedule (often monthly, per semester or annually)
legal_basis: Ed Code 48222 (the PSP, as the private school, must keep the register)
description: PSP families record attendance at home and turn it in to the PSP, which keeps the official register. Keep your own copy.

name: Attendance record (credentialed tutor)
legal_basis: Ed Code 48224
description: Document that instruction met the statutory minimum of at least 3 hours a day for 175 days each calendar year, between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m.

name: Courses of study offered
legal_basis: Ed Code 33190; Ed Code 48222, 51210, 51220 (branches of study)
description: A list of the courses/subjects offered each year (e.g., per grade: English, math, social sciences, science, fine arts, health, PE, and for grades 7-12 foreign language etc.), ideally with the curriculum/materials used. Must be kept current and available at the school.

name: Faculty names, addresses and educational qualifications
legal_basis: Ed Code 33190; Ed Code 48222 ('persons capable of teaching')
description: Names and street addresses of every teacher (usually the parent(s)) with a record of each one's educational qualifications (e.g., diploma/degree, relevant training or experience). No credential is required.

name: Immunization records or exemption status
legal_basis: H&S Code 120335; 120335(f) exempts pupils in a home-based private school and pupils in independent study (Ed Code 51745 et seq.) who receive no classroom-based instruction
description: For a PSA home school serving only the family, and for charter/district independent study with no classroom-based instruction, the school-entry immunization requirements do not apply (CDPH). Keep the child's immunization record anyway: PSPs, charters with in-person classes, co-ops held as classroom instruction, camps, and any later return to a classroom-based school will ask for it. A PSP that is not purely home-based may require records or a valid medical exemption.

name: First-grade health examination certificate or waiver (former CHDP form PM 171A/B)
deadline: Historically within 90 days after entering first grade (exam within prior 18 months)
legal_basis: H&S Code 124085 (text still in code as of Nov 2026); CHDP program ended July 1, 2024 (SB 184, 2022)
description: H&S 124085 still requires a certificate of a health screening (or a signed parent waiver) within 90 days of first-grade entry, but it is tied to the CHDP program, which was discontinued July 1, 2024; counties report the PM 171A exam form and PM 171B waiver are no longer required forms. Status for private home schools after the transition is unclear, so keep a copy of the child's well-child exam (or a signed waiver) on file. Public school students (charter/district IS) should follow their school's current instructions; a separate kindergarten/first-grade oral health assessment (Ed Code 49452.8) applies to public schools.

name: Criminal record summary / fingerprinting (Ed Code 44237)
deadline: Before the employee has contact with pupils
legal_basis: Ed Code 44237 (does not apply to a parent or legal guardian working exclusively with his or her own children)
description: Private schools must obtain a DOJ criminal record summary for employees who have contact with pupils. A parent teaching only their own children is exempt. If your home school hires a non-parent tutor/teacher or enrolls other families' children, the fingerprinting/background check requirement may apply; keep documentation.

name: Withdrawal letter to prior public school
deadline: On or before the first day of homeschooling
legal_basis: Ed Code 48222 (private school exemption); Ed Code 49068 (records transfer)
description: Short written notice to the current school that the child is withdrawing to enroll in a private school (your home-based school, or the named PSP) effective a given date. Prevents truancy follow-up. File the PSA (or enroll in the PSP) before or at the same time. Keep a dated copy and any acknowledgment.

name: Cumulative records request to prior school
legal_basis: Ed Code 49068 (records transferred on request of the new school)
description: Written request from the new school (your private home school, PSP, or charter) asking the former school to transfer the pupil's cumulative record (grades, test scores, immunization and health records, IEP/504 documents). Keep the received records in the student's file.

name: PSP enrollment forms and records release
frequency: at enrollment and usually re-enrollment each year
deadline: Set by the PSP (before the school year or before withdrawing from prior school)
legal_basis: Ed Code 33190 / 48222 (PSP files the PSA and keeps records)
description: Application/enrollment agreement, parent statement or policies acknowledgment, records request authorization, and any course plan the PSP requires. Confirm the PSP has a current-year PSA on file with CDE.

name: Course plan, grades and work logs submitted to PSP
legal_basis: Ed Code 33190 (courses of study kept by the school)
description: Lists of courses/curricula and end-of-term grades so the PSP can keep the courses-of-study record and issue report cards and high school transcripts.

name: Independent study master agreement (charter)
frequency: at enrollment; renewed per charter policy (typically each school year)
deadline: Signed before independent study instruction begins
description: Written agreement signed by the pupil, parent/guardian and supervising teacher covering learning objectives, methods of study and evaluation, how often assignments are due and evaluated, duration, resources, the right to return to classroom instruction, and required synchronous instruction/live interaction. Keep a signed copy.

name: Work samples / learning records each learning period (charter)
frequency: each learning period (commonly every 20 school days)
legal_basis: Ed Code 51747; Ed Code 51747.5 (attendance based on time value of work product); 5 CCR 11703
description: Representative samples of student work and/or assignment logs reviewed by the credentialed supervising teacher. These document attendance (ADA) for funding, so missed samples can affect enrollment status. Keep your own copies or photos.

name: Independent study agreement and work product (district)
frequency: at enrollment and per district schedule
deadline: Agreement signed before IS begins; work per district schedule
legal_basis: Ed Code 51747; 5 CCR 11700 et seq.
description: District written agreement plus completed assignments/work product evaluated by the supervising teacher. Students who fall behind trigger the district's tiered re-engagement procedures required by Ed Code 51747.

name: Instructional funds purchase requests and receipts (charter)
legal_basis: Ed Code 51747.3 (no funds or thing of value given directly to families); Ed Code 47605 (nonsectarian)
description: Requisitions/purchase orders for curriculum, classes and materials bought by the charter through approved vendors with the student's instructional funds. Items are often school property and must be secular. Keep confirmation of each order and any return-of-materials policy.

name: Copy of tutor's California teaching credential
legal_basis: Ed Code 48224
description: Proof that the tutor holds a valid California credential for the grade level taught (printout from the Commission on Teacher Credentialing credential lookup).

name: Work permit (Statement of Intent to Employ a Minor and Request for Work Permit, CDE B1-1; Permit to Employ and Work, CDE B1-4)
frequency: per job; generally renewed each school year and before the new school year starts
legal_basis: Ed Code 49110 et seq.; Labor Code 1286 et seq.
description: Minors 12-17 generally need a work permit. Per CDE's FAQ, home schools are private schools, so the principal (or designated administrator who self-certifies knowledge of child labor law) may issue permits, but a principal may NOT issue a permit to his or her own child; in that case (and if the principal declines) the local school district superintendent issues it. PSP students get permits from their PSP; charter and district IS students from their school. Entertainment permits come from the Labor Commissioner (DLSE).

name: High school transcript
deadline: Final version by graduation; needed for college applications (fall of senior year)
legal_basis: No statutory form; private schools set their own graduation requirements (Ed Code 51225.3 applies to public schools)
description: Official record of courses, credits, grades and GPA issued by the home-based private school (or by the PSP/charter for those options). Keep course descriptions and reading lists to support it. Retain permanently; former students use the school's records to obtain diplomas/transcripts.

name: High school diploma
legal_basis: Private school sets its own requirements; alternative: California High School Proficiency Exam certificate (Ed Code 48412)
description: The private school (your home school or PSP) issues its own diploma. Students 16+ (or who completed 10th grade) may also take the CHSPE, whose certificate is legally equivalent to a California high school diploma. Charter/district IS students receive their public school's diploma.

name: Student cumulative file (grades, test results, portfolio)
legal_basis: Best practice (CDE recommends keeping individual pupil records)
description: Report cards, standardized test results (if any), samples of work, reading lists, curriculum used and evaluations. Helpful for transfers back to public school, placement, college admissions, and Cal Grant/financial aid documentation.

name: State testing and Physical Fitness Test notes
legal_basis: Ed Code 60640 (CAASPP) and 60800 (Physical Fitness Test) apply to public schools including charters; not to private schools
description: PSA, PSP and tutor students are not required to take CAASPP or the Physical Fitness Test (PFT). Charter and district independent study students participate in CAASPP and, in grades 5, 7 and 9, the PFT. Private homeschoolers may still choose a nationally normed test for their own records.

name: Sample letters: withdrawal, records request, notice of exemption
description: Templates for a withdrawal letter to the former public school, a cumulative records request from your private school, and a short response to a district or attendance officer inquiry citing Ed Code 48222 and your PSA filing. HSLDA and statewide homeschool organizations publish examples (some member-only).

name: Proof of high school completion for financial aid (homeschool)
deadline: Cal Grant GPA/test verification by March 2 of senior year; FAFSA/CADAA opens Oct 1
legal_basis: 20 U.S.C. 1091(d) (homeschool completion recognized for federal aid when state treats it as a home or private school); CSAC Cal Grant rules
description: Keep the final transcript and diploma, plus SAT/ACT or other test scores. Homeschool graduates may substitute accepted test scores for a GPA for Cal Grant purposes, and colleges may request a transcript as proof of homeschool completion for federal aid.
